newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures firmer in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures firmer in line with JGBs.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were slightly higher in late Thursday trade, in line with gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, which shrugged off concerns about the early passage of a supplementary budget.

"Talk of the additional budget is usually negative for JGBs. But the economy is not showing any progress and the stock market's still not doing well so where's the money going to go apart from bonds," said a Japanese bank dealer.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters the early passage of a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year was expected to have a favourable effect on the economy.
Dealers said Euroyen futures were also supported by news of a 9.7 percent month-on-month drop in private-sector machinery orders for November, after a 44.2 percent rise in October.
"It tends to be quite a volatile number but its going into negative territory does support Euroyen," said a dealer with a U.S. house.
But he added that September Euroyen was having trouble climbing above 99.33. The Japanese bank dealer said the contract would face resistance around its high of 99.36.
It was quoted at 99.32 at 1125 GMT against its IMM close at 99.30. March JGBs ended at 126.15 against their opening 125.45.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed following overnight losses in U.S. treasuries where a heavy supply of corporate debt weighed on the market.
"There is a bit of nervousness coming in about when the Fed might make a move. People do seem to expect a rate hike this year. They're just not sure when," said the U.S. house trader.
He said any strength in U.S. economic data was likely to trigger fears of an imminent move by the Federal Reserve and cause a sell-off in Eurodollars.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.38 against their IMM close at 94.37. June was unchanged at 94.19
